`toMicros` used `Math.floor(usd * 1_000_000)`. Binary floating point stores many decimal amounts just below their true value (`2.01 * 1e6` is `2009999.9999999998`), so floor dropped a micro-dollar from those turns: a $2.01 turn was stored as 2009999. It now uses `Math.round`. Any USD amount with at most six decimal places lands within a tiny fraction of a micro of its integer, so rounding recovers it exactly. Do not switch back to floor or `Math.trunc` to "avoid overcharging". Neither one is more conservative, because both just carry the float error forward.

Zenith doesn't retry a turn once it has failed partway through. Retries happen only in the HTTP transport layer (`crates/agent-transport/src/retry.rs`), and only when no side effect can have happened yet: connection failures before the first response byte, or 429/529 responses that carry `Retry-After`. Anything that fails after the first content block marks the turn as failed and shows the user what the agent did so far with a Resume button. This replaced an older loop that resent the whole transcript up to 3 times, which re-ran tool calls that had already executed and produced things like duplicate commits.
